statement: Recent-graduate unemployment minus the all-worker rate >= 2.0 pp in any 2027 quarter (NY Fed College Labor Market; 2027 quarterly)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2023. Last in-phase reading (Sept 2023 data, posted Nov 2023): recent-graduate unemployment 4.4% vs 3.6% for all workers, a gap of ~0.8 pp. The inversion (recent graduates above all workers) drew press attention, but the gap was far below 2.0 pp. Q4 2023 data were posted in Feb 2024 and are excluded.

items.summary: Major newspaper report, citing a Bloc A regional central bank's September 2023 data: recent college graduates were more likely to be unemployed than the overall workforce, a reversal of long-held norms.
items.detail: Bloc A Post, 'New college grads are more likely to be unemployed in today's job market', 2023-11-19 (verified via web_extract this run; body mostly paywalled, headline and lede captured), based on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York College Labor Market data.

items.summary: Magazine analysis of the same data: as of September 2023, recent-graduate (ages 22-27) unemployment was 4.4% vs 3.6% for all workers, a 0.8 pp gap; the two rates had moved within a percentage point of each other for a decade.
items.detail: The Atlantic, 'The Myth of the Unemployed College Grad', Dec 2023 (exact day approximate) (verified via web_extract this run), citing NY Fed College Labor Market data. Gap 0.8 pp vs the 2.0 pp threshold.

items.summary: Primary series: the regional central bank's recent-graduate unemployment data file (opened this run; current vintage only, so in-phase values are taken from the dated secondary reports above).
items.detail: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, The Labor Market for Recent College Graduates, unemployment data CSV (verified reachable via web_extract this run; extract truncated before 2023 rows and file reflects later revisions, so no value recorded from it). Release month approximate (quarterly, typically November for Q3).
